evidence_excerpts: Less than 25% of meditation trials actively assess adverse effects, compared to 100% of pharmacology trials, and many rely on spontaneous reporting that may underestimate adverse-effect frequency by more than 20-fold.
The article states that the assumption of minimal adverse effects associated with meditation is largely based on a lack of research rather than substantive evidence.
text: Meditation-related adverse effects are under-assessed in current trials, so claims that meditation is free of adverse effects rest on inadequate evidence.
